evidence.detail: Repository HEAD exactly matches the launcher-supplied target commit.
The target record exists and identifies itself as roadmap v4, a draft awaiting this review and exact human approval.
The working tree was clean (`git status --short` produced no entries).
The governance validator could not execute because the read-only environment offered no writable temporary directory; it exited 1 before producing validation results.

The review covered the approved brief v2, roadmap v4, M2 work items ISSUE-0007 through ISSUE-0011 embedded in the roadmap, DECISION-014, current workflow status, existing auth/server architecture, and relevant security boundaries.

evidence: AGENTS.md requires real governance validation evidence and says missing or unverifiable non-security evidence blocks a review.
The validator exited 1 with `FileNotFoundError: No usable temporary directory found` while creating its smoke-test temporary directory.
No successful governance-validation result for target commit faf5ec70bf00d364c848be057e6422905e337619 was available in this isolated review.
findings.remediation: Rerun the plan review in a read-only checkout that provides a separate writable temporary directory, or supply independently captured validator evidence bound to this exact target commit under the repository's documented evidence policy.
findings.title: Required governance validation could not be executed
findings.verification: Run `python3 scripts/validate_repo.py` against faf5ec70bf00d364c848be057e6422905e337619 and record exit status 0 and relevant output.

evidence: ISSUE-0009 requires only presence and type validation for `tenant`, `client_id`, and `client_secret`.

The existing server accepts request bodies up to 64 KiB, so presence/type checks alone permit extremely large credential fields to reach validation, encoding, retained process memory, and the identity transport.
The roadmap describes tenant syntax but gives no explicit length limits, and it gives neither syntax nor length criteria for client IDs or secrets.
findings.remediation: Add bounded validation criteria for all three app-auth fields before retention or outbound transport. Define tenant length together with GUID/DNS rules, require the client ID format expected by Entra, and set a documented defensible secret-length bound while preserving valid Entra secrets. Require boundary tests proving oversized and malformed values return 400 without transport invocation or secret retention.
findings.title: App-auth input validation is unbounded and underspecified
findings.verification: Review ISSUE-0009 criteria for explicit format/length bounds and run tests covering minimum, maximum, malformed, and oversized inputs; mocks must prove rejected inputs cause no identity request and leave no app-only state.

evidence: The architecture requires provider error text to be truncated and scrubbed only for an occurrence of the submitted secret.
ISSUE-0008 similarly tests provider error text containing the literal secret, while ISSUE-0009 promises stable machine-label errors.
Literal replacement does not cover transformed representations such as URL encoding, JSON escaping, partial reflection, or normalization, despite provider response bodies being untrusted input.
Returning only stable local error labels already satisfies the stated operational requirement and avoids relying on incomplete redaction.
findings.remediation: Remove provider-supplied error descriptions from all client-visible and logged output; map failures to stable locally defined labels. If diagnostic provider text must be retained, explicitly justify it and specify/test encoded and transformed secret variants, but omission is the smaller and safer plan.
findings.title: Literal-only scrubbing is not a sufficient boundary for untrusted provider errors
findings.verification: Mock provider errors containing the secret literally, URL-encoded, JSON-escaped, split, and surrounded by diagnostic text; assert responses, exceptions, logs, stderr, and manager representations contain only stable local labels and no provider description or secret representation.

evidence: The roadmap's project outcome still describes only device-code authentication and says no client secret is required, without distinguishing the new optional app-only outcome.
The stakeholder table still says tenant consent requires no standing app registration, although M2 explicitly serves an owner with an existing consented app registration.
The project definition of done still says `M1 = the whole MVP`, which makes final project status after adding M2 ambiguous.
findings.remediation: Update the top-level project outcome, stakeholder/success table, and project definition of done to describe both modes and clarify whether M2 is an extension after the completed MVP or part of the current project's completion scope.
findings.title: Top-level roadmap narrative remains stale after adding M2
findings.verification: Read the roadmap without relying on later M2 sections and confirm it accurately states the default device-code path, optional app-only prerequisite and secret, and the exact meaning of project completion.

limitations: The governance validator could not run because the review sandbox had no writable temporary directory; this is an environment limitation, not evidence that the validator or roadmap is defective.
No live Microsoft tenant, real client secret, or network authentication was used. The roadmap intentionally treats live behavior for A1, A2, A6, and A7 as protected, residual evidence gaps.
ISSUE-0007 through ISSUE-0011 do not yet exist as separate issue records; this review evaluated their complete proposed definitions as embedded in ROADMAP.md.
Implementation tests and compile checks were not treated as plan evidence because M2 code does not exist yet and the review environment is read-only.
review.summary: Target identity is correct and the M2 sequence is broadly feasible, but the review is blocked by unavailable governance-validation evidence. Before approval, the roadmap also needs bounded app-auth input criteria and a safer rule that never exposes untrusted provider error descriptions. The top-level roadmap narrative should be synchronized with the new dual-mode scope.
